claims.claim: Claude Opus 5 launched July 24, 2026 at $5/Mtok input and $25/Mtok output, unchanged from Opus 4.8
Opus 5 ships a five-level effort ladder (low/medium/high/xhigh/max, default high); thinking cannot be disabled at xhigh/max
Anthropic's own effort-ladder data shows Frontier-Bench score peaking at xhigh (44.4%) and dipping slightly at max, making the top of the ladder non-monotonic
Epoch AI scores Opus 5 at ECI 159 (90% CI 157-162) vs Fable 5 at 161; on SWE-ECI the two tie at 161

Epoch AI's own methodology states absolute ECI values are not meaningful in isolation; roughly 5 ECI points equate to one doubling of METR's autonomous-task time horizon, making a 2-point gap far below that unit

"FrontierCode" is Cognition's own 150-task/36-repo coding benchmark (50-task 'Diamond' hard subset), unrelated to Epoch's ECI; a Cognition team member conceded under Hacker News scrutiny that ~50+ runs per model would be needed for statistical confidence versus the ~5 actually run

Independent benchmark CodeRabbit found Opus 5's effort dial behaves as a precision/recall trade rather than uniform improvement: x-high effort raised precision from 35.2% to 39.3% while recall fell from 61.1% to 55.2%

Anthropic Fellows Program research (arXiv:2507.14417) documents Claude reasoning models becoming more distracted by irrelevant context the longer they reason ("inverse scaling in test-time compute"), predating Opus 5

Non-monotonic effort/reasoning-budget scaling is documented across other frontier models, not unique to Opus 5: GPT-5 Thinking peaks at medium and declines at high on the FrontierCS benchmark; Gemini 2.5 Pro's lowest thinking-budget setting outscores all higher tiers on TaxCalcBench; a DeepSeek-R1-Distill model shows a full inverted-U on GSM-8K

Claude 3.7 Sonnet (a predecessor generation) already showed inverse reasoning-effort scaling on a biosecurity benchmark subtask while o3-mini scaled monotonically on the same suite, showing the pattern is neither new to Claude nor universal across vendors

Anthropic's support documentation: the cyber-classifier fallback to Opus 4.8 triggers on exploit generation, binary-based vulnerability scanning, and penetration testing, and scans everything the model reads in-session (memory, connectors, web search, files), not just the latest message
There is no fallback model at all for biology/chemistry/life-sciences-flagged requests; Opus 5 applies safeguards similar to Opus 4.8, implying refusal rather than substitution

In consumer surfaces (Claude.ai, Claude Code, Cowork) a fallback is visible by default: the user sees a notice, the response is labeled with the model that answered, and the picker stays on Opus 4.8 for the rest of the conversation until manually switched back

Automatic fallback is opt-in for the raw API (developers must configure a beta header and a fallbacks parameter); by default an unconfigured API call that trips a classifier returns a plain HTTP 200 refusal, not a silent swap

When fallback is configured, the API response's top-level model field always names the model that actually answered, and usage.iterations records the handoff — Anthropic maintains a dedicated cookbook guide because developers were observed not checking this field, and a documented GitHub issue shows a third-party client (oh-my-pi) parsing none of the three available signals

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic's Fable 5 model card disclosed that safeguards limiting the model's usefulness for frontier-LLM-development requests would be invisible to users and would not fall back to a different model; within roughly a day of public backlash (dubbed "secret sabotage"), Anthropic reversed the secrecy so these refusals fall back openly with a stated reason, while the underlying restriction itself stayed in place
Anthropic states it expects the cyber-classifiers to intervene approximately 85% less often for Opus 5 than they did for Fable 5, based on internal testing ("we expect"), not an external audit

Anthropic's automated behavioral audit scores Opus 5 at 2.3 on overall misaligned behavior (lower is better) versus 2.85 for Opus 4.8, 2.81 for Mythos 5, and 3.35 for Sonnet 5, and calls Opus 5 its "most aligned model to date" on this self-graded, internal metric

No independent alignment/scheming evaluation of Opus 5 specifically (from Apollo Research, METR, or similar) had been published as of one day post-launch; the UK AI Security Institute's contribution to the system card covers offensive cyber-capability testing (8 of 10 attempts succeeded against a weak-security network range), not the self-graded alignment claims

Harvey (legal AI) cites 26% fewer tokens at Opus 4.8 max-reasoning parity, corroborated same-day on Harvey's own blog with an internal 11.7% all-pass score on its proprietary Legal Agent Benchmark; Fundamental Research Lab's 9pp-accuracy/60%-less-time claim and Zapier's AutomationBench "topped leaderboard" claim each appear only inside Anthropic's own launch post with no independent third-party corroboration found

Zapier's public AutomationBench leaderboard uses a private held-out evaluation set distinct from its open 600-task GitHub/arXiv release, and Opus 5's best overall pass rate on the public leaderboard was roughly 26% at launch — meaning "topped the leaderboard" describes leading a weak field, not high absolute task competence

No binding regulation (EU AI Act, FINRA, SEC, NIST AI RMF, ABA/state bar ethics opinions) currently requires disclosure of mid-session AI model-version substitution; commentary frames FTC deception doctrine as the only theoretically applicable, untested framework

Anthropic's disclosed annualized revenue run-rate reached roughly $47 billion by May 2026 (up from about $9 billion at end-2025), with a $965 billion primary Series H valuation and secondary-market marks as high as $1.2 trillion by July 2026

Anthropic shipped four distinct model tiers in under two months before Opus 5: Mythos 5 and Fable 5 (June 9, 2026) and Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026), positioning Opus 5 explicitly as the cost-efficient "daily driver" rather than a capability-crown release, amid GLM-5.2 undercutting Claude Opus-tier output pricing by roughly 5-6x

Google's Gemini CLI documents a silent internal-utility fallback chain, but this is health/availability-triggered routing for background calls, not content-classifier-triggered downgrade of the user-facing model; OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol offers an explicit opt-in retry-on-lower-capability-model path rather than an automatic silent swap; no public reporting confirms an OpenAI or Google mechanism directly analogous to Opus 5's classifier-triggered fallback
